name: Lucky Danger
hours: Tue–Thu 11:30 a.m.–2 p.m. and 4:30–9 p.m.; Fri 11:30 a.m.–2 p.m. and 4:30–10 p.m.; Sat 4:30–10 p.m.; closed Sun–Mon
hours_source: Official site, luckydanger.co/washington-dc, fetched Nov 26, 2026
group_notes: Mahjong room bookable by the hour; private classes for up to 15
location: 7th and D St NW, three blocks south of the Chinatown boundary.
blurb: Tim Ma's love letter to American Chinese takeout has traveled a long way: a 2020 pandemic pop-up, an Arlington takeout spot from 2021 and, since June 2025, this full-service flagship. Executive chef Robbie Reyes treats the canon (General Tso's chicken, beef and broccoli, crab rangoon) as something worth reworking, not apologizing for. Come for the cocktail bars; stay for the back mahjong room and its three automatic shuffling tables, billed as DC's only public one.

name: Cinnara
cuisine_detail: Chinese (Southwest Chinese beef noodles, individual hot pots)
hours: Daily 11 a.m.–9:30 p.m.
hours_source: Official site eatcinnara.com, fetched Nov 26, 2026
blurb: Formerly Bonkers' Chinese Burger, this 6th Street counter has turned toward Southwest China as a noodle and hot pot shop. Everything hinges on a slow-simmered beef bone broth, the base for its signature beef noodles (Mala Spicy Beef Noodle Soup and Taiwan Braised Beef Noodle Soup among them). Individual hot pots draw on Sichuan, Chongqing, Guizhou and Yunnan flavors; handmade dumplings, pork wontons and fresh fruit teas round it out. Open daily, 11 AM to 9:30 PM.

blurb: Luna Hall's anchor, and the reason many people walk in: soup dumplings (xiao long bao) in pork, chicken, mala spicy pork, crab and pork, shrimp and zucchini, and black truffle. Can't choose? blurb: TKK has been frying chicken since 1974, when its first shop opened in Taipei's Ximending. Here it comes as mixed buckets, sandwiches or tenders, in original, crispy mild or crispy spicy, with curly fries alongside. The Infatuation (Nov 2023) scored it 8.5 and pointed straight at the tenders. It shares a counter with Kung Fu Tea.
